MUQATIL:76:23-26/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:76:23-26/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:76:23-26/r5.claim: Remembering God at dawn means the Fajr prayer and at evening the Maghrib prayer, with three takbirs and testimony to God's oneness at each; this repudiates shirk.

ZAJJAJ:v5p263#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p263#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p263#2/r1.claim: Aṣīl means evening; aṣalnā means they entered the evening.

NAHHAS:v5p106/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p106/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p106/r6.claim: Bakratan is indefinite and declinable here, paired with indefinite aṣīlan; it is definite only with the article.

THALABI:v10p106/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p106/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p106/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord morning and evening means the two evening prayers; prostrating at night and long night glorification mean voluntary night prayer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r2.claim: Remembering God's name morning and evening means the morning prayer, then the noon and afternoon prayers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means affirming his oneness in prayer.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r2.speaker: عطاء والكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r2.claim: Morning and evening refer to the dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p299/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p299/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p299/r1.claim: Remember God morning and evening; night prostrations refer to Maghrib and Isha, while extended night glorification means voluntary prayer after obligatory prayer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r3.claim: ذكر اسم ربك means persistent remembrance morning and evening; at night it means prostration and prayer, or saying سبحان الله.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r4.speaker: ابن حبيب وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r4.claim: Some scholars map the times to the five prayers: dawn, noon and afternoon, then sunset and night.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say this command was obligatory and then abrogated; only the five daily prayers remain obligatory.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r6.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p414#2/r6.claim: Another group says the command remains recommended.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means affirming His oneness in prayer; bukr means dawn prayer, and aṣīl means afternoon prayer, or noon and afternoon prayers together.

RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.claim: One reading takes morning and evening remembrance as the five prayers: dawn, noon and afternoon, sunset and night; the long night glorification is night vigil.

RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r4.claim: A second reading takes the command as verbal and inward praise, requiring remembrance of God by heart and tongue at all times, as in 33:41-42.

RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r5.claim: After the gift of revelation and guidance, the Prophet is told to obey God alone; knowing divine names and attributes is possible, but created minds cannot reach the divine essence.

RAZI-FULL:v30p228/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p228/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p228/r5.claim: After forbidding obedience to wrongdoers, God commands remembering His name in the morning and evening, prostrating at night, and glorifying Him through a long night.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r2.claim: Remembering God morning and evening means praying at the start and end of the day: dawn, then noon and afternoon prayers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:25/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:25/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:25/r1.claim: Maintain remembrance at morning and evening, or keep the dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers, since الأصيل includes both later times.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#5/r1.claim: Remembering God's name means prayer: morning is Fajr and early evening means Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr.

QASHANI:76:23-25/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:76:23-25/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:76:23-25/r4.claim: Remembering the Lord’s name means realizing one’s own Essence as God’s greatest Name and manifesting its rights and perfections from primordial beginning to end.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p294/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p294/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p294/r2.claim: Remembering God morning and evening means at the beginning and end of the day.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r1.claim: Avoiding outward and inward sin requires avoiding each kind; if unbelievers invite the Prophet to something involving neither sin nor disbelief, he may accept.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r2.claim: Unhindered remembrance of God is the remedy for spiritual harm and precedes worship, since knowing God is worship’s aim and thought joined to worship is its highest form.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r3.claim: Morning remembrance follows waking, a minor death, and recalls resurrection; evening remembrance recalls the world’s ending, while naming both times signals continual remembrance.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r4.claim: Remembering God’s name may command prayer, the best bodily worship because it joins tongue, heart, and limbs in ordered acts that affirm the Creator’s existence and oneness.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r5.claim: One possible reading prescribes dawn and afternoon prayers, which were the only prayers commanded early in Islam and were then two cycles each.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276/r6.claim: Alternatively, the command includes dawn, noon, and afternoon, since the broad term for evening covers the latter two; other prayers are included in the following phrase.

BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r3.claim: Remember the Lord from morning to evening, meaning continue remembrance at all times; the two times may also stand for Fajr, Zuhr, and Asr prayers.

BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r4.claim: Asil can extend from after Asr to sunset, or from noon onward, covering Zuhr and Asr.

BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r5.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r5.claim: Saʿdi al-Mufti says a continuous-remembrance interpretation is needed only if the five prayers had not already been prescribed before this verse; he assumes they had been prescribed at the Ascension.

BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p213#3/r6.claim: Bursevi questions that assumption: the Ascension preceded the Hijra by a year, but the verse’s date is unknown, so the argument works only if it came afterward.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p166/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166/r1.claim: Remember God's name morning and evening, or maintain the Fajr and Zuhr prayers, since الأصيل can include the period from noon to sunset.

ELMALILI:76:25-31/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r1.claim: “Bukra” covers early morning through noon and “aṣīl” afternoon through evening; together the command spans the day and includes morning, noon, and afternoon prayers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord's name includes proclaiming the message, obligatory and voluntary worship, and exhorting people through fear of punishment and hope for reward.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r2.claim: ‘Morning and evening’ covers the day's set prayer times as well as voluntary prayer, supplication, and seeking forgiveness; the terms mean early day and late day.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r7.claim: They read morning and evening as the five prescribed prayers and their times, taking ‘evening’ to include noon; glorification then points to night prayer.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r8.claim: These instructions echo commands to glorify God, prostrate, remember Him, and persevere despite opponents' words.

ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n23/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n23/r1.claim: Remembering God's name means recalling His attributes as manifested in creation; human beings can grasp His existence and attributes, but not the nature of His Reality, as Razi explains.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.claim: The Prophet should persevere despite opponents, trust God, and seek patience through prayer and remembrance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.claim: Disbelievers' real ailment is unwillingness to sacrifice immediate gains for the Hereafter; they fabricate objections despite its certainty, though recreating them is easy for God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r1.claim: Morning and evening remembrance and worship strengthen the Prophet's devotion, resolve, and resistance to the polytheists' attacks.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r2.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r2.claim: One reported view takes remembrance as the five daily prayers: morning means dawn prayer, evening means noon and afternoon prayers, night prostration means sunset and night prayers, and extended night prayer is obligatory for the Prophet but recommended for his community.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r3.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r3.claim: A second reported view understands morning and evening remembrance as verbal glorification and belief in God's transcendence throughout day and night, rather than prayer alone.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r4.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r4.claim: A third view includes all these forms of remembrance: obligatory prayer, voluntary prayer, supplication, and seeking forgiveness.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r5.claim: The author takes the verses broadly as stressing worship and devotion, especially prayer at parts of the night alongside glorification, supplication, repentance, and seeking forgiveness.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r1.claim: After commanding patience and forbidding obedience to sinners and ingrates, God commands abundant remembrance; the author links remembrance to moments requiring patience and crisis.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r2.claim: The Qur'an links glorification with distress and struggle: it follows the Prophet's constricted heart and accompanies steadfastness in battle.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p350/r3.claim: Jonah's continued glorification saved him from remaining in the whale; remembrance and glorification are among the purest, highest deeds, so they follow distress logically.

STUDYQURAN:76:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r1.speaker: Aj, JJ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r1.claim: The verses may enjoin naming God in the daily prayers; Aj also reads them as remembrance of God at every moment.

STUDYQURAN:76:25/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r2.claim: In context, the command counsels remembering God amid worldly tribulations; many Sufis take verse 25 as invoking God’s Supreme Name, Allāh.
